evals.prompt: How long did docs/plans/2026-09-02-sample-refactor-plan.md actually take? I feel like it dragged.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs telemetry.py report on the plan, checks the coverage line and the --sessions listing for false positives, then reports attended vs agent-busy time, prompts, autonomous-run median and the findings.
assertions: scripts/telemetry.py report is run with the plan file as its argument
The answer distinguishes attended time from agent-busy time
The answer cites at least one finding or states that none fired
No transcript text, prompt or session title is quoted

evals.prompt: Why was this plan so slow — was the work hard or was it the process?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the report and reads it through the task-vs-process lens: busy/attended, autonomous runs, stop classes, resume KB and per-task shares.
assertions: The answer states whether task slowness or process slowness dominates and names the numbers behind it
Per-task shares are cited when one task exceeds 30% of active time

evals.prompt: The plan is COMPLETED. Close out its session telemetry and add it to the ledger.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs telemetry.py close on the plan, which writes the subject JSON and upserts one ledger row under the user-level storage, then pastes the printed summary into the archive stub or Final Verification.
assertions: scripts/telemetry.py close is run with the plan file
Nothing is written inside the repository except the pasted summary
The summary is at most 5 lines

evals.prompt: Compare plan performance before and after the manual-planning 2.1 change. Did it help?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs telemetry.py baseline, reports medians per Plan Format cohort, and refuses to conclude for any cohort under 3 plans.
assertions: Only medians are reported, never means
A cohort with fewer than 3 plans is reported as 'do not conclude'
Quality guards (reverts, TODOs) are mentioned alongside the friction numbers

evals.prompt: Show me the session telemetry sources on this machine — is OpenCode being picked up?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs telemetry.py sources and reports which stores exist, their shape and session counts.

evals.prompt: Our API endpoint is slow — can you profile the request handler?
evals.expected_output: A code profiling task. session-telemetry is not used: it measures coding sessions, not application performance.

evals.prompt: Add OpenTelemetry tracing to the checkout service.
evals.expected_output: An application instrumentation task; the word telemetry refers to the product, not to agent sessions.

evals.prompt: Show me the last prompt I sent in yesterday's session.
evals.expected_output: session-telemetry never prints prompts or transcript text, so it is not the tool for this; the agent answers by other means or explains where transcripts live.
assertions: scripts/telemetry.py is not run to retrieve prompt text
